chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Ahmad ibn Rizq-Allah, from Yahya ibn al-’Ala, from Jabir, from Abi Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:

A servant remained in the Fire for seventy autumns, and the autumn is seventy years. He then said: 'O Lord! Have mercy on me for the sake of Muhammad and his family.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Jibraeel: 'Descend to My servant and bring him out.' Jibraeel asked: 'O Lord, how should I descend into the Fire?' Allah said: 'I have commanded it to be cool for you and safe.' He asked: 'O Lord, inform me of his location.' Allah said: 'He is in a well in Sijjil.' Jibraeel descended upon the Fire, face down, and brought him out. Allah said: 'O My servant, how long did you remain in the Fire?' He replied: 'I cannot count it, O Lord.' Allah said to him: 'By My Honor, if you had not asked Me by this means, I would have prolonged your humiliation in the Fire. But I have decreed upon Myself that no servant of Mine asks Me for the sake of Muhammad and his family but that I forgive what is between Me and him. And I have forgiven you today.'

key_terms.حَتَمْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي: I decreed upon Myself (obligated by divine promise)
key_terms.سِجِّيلٌ: Sijjil (a place or well in Hell)

ai.seo_question: How does supplicating by the right of Muhammad and his family affect punishment in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq illustrates the profound efficacy of *tawassul* through the *haqq* (right/authority) of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, demonstrating that such intercession can mitigate even prolonged punishment in Hellfire. The narrative highlights Allah’s self-imposed obligation (*hamt*) to forgive those who supplicate by this right, reinforcing the Shia belief in the spiritual authority of the Imams as mediators of divine mercy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Hassan b. Ali from al-Abbas b. ’Amir from Ahmad b. Rizq-Allah from Yahya b. al-’Ala from Jabir from Abi Ja’far (a.s.)

who said: ‘O Lord! Have mercy on me for the sake of Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) and his progeny’ Allah will order Jibraeel (a.s.) to go down and grant salvation to him. Jibraeel (a.s.) will ask, ‘How should I get down in fire?’ Allah will say: I have ordered it to remain cool for you and you will not be harmed. Jibraeel (a.s.) will ask, ‘O Lord! Tell me where is that servant of Yours?’ Allah will say that he is in the well of Sijjil. Jibraeel (a.s.) will go there and remove him from fire. Allah will ask, ‘O slave of Mine! For how long did you remain there?’ He will reply, ‘O Lord! It is not possible for me to estimate it’. Allah will swear by His Honor and say: I would have kept you in Hell in the same state if you hadn’t prayed to Me in this way. I have made it obligatory for Myself to forgive any number of sins of one who supplicates in the name of Muhammad (s.a.w.s.) and his progeny just like I forgave you this day.”
